title: Grade 2 Science — Tue, Jun 17
description: Our Food — Day 2 of 5: Food from animals
subject: science

questions.question: We get milk from:
questions.explanation: We get milk from cows, buffaloes, goats, and camels. Milk is rich in calcium and protein.

questions.question: Eggs that we eat usually come from:
questions.explanation: Most eggs we eat come from hens. Duck and quail eggs are also eaten in some places.

questions.question: Honey is made by:
questions.explanation: Honey bees collect nectar from flowers and make honey in their hives. Honey is a natural sweetener.

questions.question: Which food is made from milk?
questions.explanation: Curd (dahi) is made from milk by adding a small amount of curd to warm milk and letting it set. Butter, cheese, and paneer are also milk products.

questions.question: Fish and prawns are food that comes from:
questions.explanation: Fish and prawns live in water — rivers, lakes, and the sea. They are a rich source of protein.

questions.question: Ghee (clarified butter) is made from:
questions.explanation: Ghee is made by heating butter (which comes from milk) until the water evaporates, leaving pure fat.

questions.question: Which of these is an animal food product?
questions.explanation: Paneer (cottage cheese) is made from milk — an animal product. Wheat, mustard, and sugarcane are plants.

questions.question: Silk thread for making silk cloth comes from:
questions.explanation: Silkworms spin a cocoon made of one long silk thread. Silk is a natural fibre from an animal.

questions.question: Which gives us both milk AND meat?
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk (dairy product) and are also a source of meat (in non-vegetarian diets). Hens give eggs and chicken meat.

questions.question: Why is milk important for growing children?
options: It gives energy from sugar only
It is rich in calcium, which makes bones and teeth strong
questions.explanation: Milk is rich in calcium and protein. Calcium is essential for building strong bones and teeth in growing children.

questions.question: Butter is made by churning ___.
questions.explanation: Butter is made by churning cream (the fat layer on top of milk) until the fat separates.

questions.question: Which animal gives us wool for making warm clothes?
questions.explanation: Wool comes from sheep. Their thick fleece is sheared, cleaned, and spun into yarn for sweaters and blankets.

questions.question: A person who eats both plant food and animal food is called a:
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Humans are omnivores. Herbivores eat only plants; carnivores eat only animals.

questions.question: Prawn, crab, and lobster are all ___.
questions.explanation: Prawns, crabs, and lobsters are crustaceans — sea animals that are eaten as food in coastal areas.

questions.question: Which two products come from cows?
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk (for dairy products) and cow dung, which is used as natural fertiliser and dried as fuel in villages.
